item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mostly no. There is real evidence of development-oriented statecraft in 2024, but the strongest pattern is mixed macro stewardship plus some prestige/patronage-heavy project choices, not a clear commitment to broad-based, sustainable prosperity over rent extraction or short-term political gain.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Bangladesh: Country Partnership Report / development progress snapshot](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099514001022413953) — World Bank, December 31, 2023, disclosed January 2, 2024.  
  Claim: The World Bank described “remarkable development progress,” including lower-middle-income status, gender parity in school enrollment, and large mortality reductions. This is the best positive evidence that the state was pursuing broad social development rather than pure extraction, though it is background and not proof of 2024 intent by itself.  
  Question IDs: `5B.1`

- [NAP Expo 2024 highlights need for new approach to adaptation planning and support](https://unfccc.int/news/nap-expo-2024-highlights-need-for-new-approach-to-adaptation-planning-and-support) — UNFCCC, April 24, 2024.  
  Claim: Bangladesh hosted NAP Expo 2024 and was described as a leader in adaptation planning with improved cyclone resilience. This supports a long-horizon, public-goods-oriented prosperity strategy, but it is sector-specific and not enough on its own to show broad-based prosperity was prioritized over politics.  
  Question IDs: `5B.1`

- [Financial sector and fiscal policy reforms will help Bangladesh sustain strong growth despite strong growth South Asia](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r) — World Bank, April 2, 2024.  
  Claim: The World Bank said growth momentum remained favorable, but high inflation eroded purchasing power, reserves were under pressure, and reforms were needed. This is negative evidence that the 2024 stewardship environment was not cleanly aligned with broad-based, sustainable prosperity.  
  Question IDs: `5B.1`

- [Bangladeshs nuclear prestige illusion](https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/views/news/bangladeshs-nuclear-prestige-illusion-3590666) — The Daily Star, April 20, 2024.  
  Claim: This opinion piece argued the push for a second Rooppur plant looked prestige-driven amid debt and inflation. That supports the interpretation that short-term image and political signaling were competing with sustainable prosperity.  
  Question IDs: `5B.1`

- [Bangla Outlook on Rooppur cost inflation and linked contracts](https://en.banglaoutlook.org/news/1099) — Bangla Outlook, April 23, 2024.  
  Claim: The article alleged major cost inflation and politically linked ancillary contracts around Rooppur. If accurate, that points toward patronage and rent-seeking dynamics rather than broad-based development discipline.  
  Question IDs: `5B.1`

- [Rooppur Power Plant was AL govts white elephant energy sector experts](https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801) — TBS News, October 5, 2024.  
  Claim: Energy-sector experts described Rooppur as a white-elephant project tied to mismanagement and corruption under the Awami League government. This is strong negative evidence that some major spending decisions were not optimized for sustainable prosperity.  
  Question IDs: `5B.1`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a strong 2024 source showing Hasina explicitly chose broad-based prosperity over loyalty-buying or rent extraction.
- The strongest positive material is macro-development and climate-adaptation oriented, but it is mostly background or sector-specific.
- The strongest negative material is not just recessionary pressure; it is the pattern of prestige-driven or patronage-prone project governance, especially around Rooppur, alongside inflation and reserve strain.
